newsitem.title: USA: Bulgaria met Feb debt service - former cenbanker.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria met Feb debt service - former cenbanker.

text.p: Bulgaria paid up its debt service for January and February, but the challenge remained to meet payments for the remainder of the year, said Todor Vulchev, former chairman of the Bulgarian central bank.

Vulchev told a press briefing arranged through Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in New York that Bulgaria needs $1 billion a year for debt service, and progress is being made in securing a standby agreement from the International Monetary Fund.
More help is also expected from the World Bank and the European Union, he said.
Asked if Bulgaria was behind in February payment, Vulchev responded, "No."
Vulchev, who served as chairman of Bulgaria's central bank from 1991 to January 1997, said Bulgaria paid $174 million in January and the February payment was very small.
"The government is convinced that a default would be a disaster," he said. "It will isolate Bulgaria from the financial markets.
The real test will come in July and December, when the Ministry of Finance must face millions more in foreign debt service obligations, Volchev said.

By then, however, Bulgaria would have weathered the political crisis, and secured multilateral financing to meet the payment, he said, adding that the country has positive balance of trade and current account.
As part of the standby agreement with the IMF, Bulgaria would adopt a currency board.
"I am absolutely sure a currency board will be created in the second quarter," he said, noting that some laws must be enacted by the parliament to allow the currency board to take effect.

Volchev predicted the United Democratic Forces, which composed of four parties, would win the parliamentary election in April, thus ending the present chaos and putting the country back on track of market reforms.
